What this is

A first-of-its-kind youth music education workshop for North East India

Over six immersive days, young musicians from across the Seven Sisters states train with international faculty in technique, theory, interpretation and performance — then take it to a public stage on the final evening. It is the first step in building long-term music education partnerships for students from the region, with the aim of creating lasting academic links to institutions such as Trinity Laban and the Yehudi Menuhin School, while celebrating the distinctive musical heritage of the Seven Sisters.

The workshop is anchored by Bernardi Music Group (UK), in collaboration with the Global Assamese Engagement Initiative and the Alliance for Community Capacity Building in NE India.

Access

Open pathways for talented young people across North East India, including scholarships and subsidised places.

Excellence

Conservatoire-style teaching in technique, theory, interpretation and performance.

Community

Enduring relationships between North East India and the UK and global music networks.

Who is teaching

Distinguished faculty

Andrew Bernardi

Violin, viola & director

Leading UK violinist, festival director and founder of Bernardi Music Group. He has performed with the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and BBC Philharmonic.

Belinda Jones

Piano

A solo, duo and chamber music pianist based in London who has performed across the world and works as a pianist for Southbank Centre.

Jonathan Few

Cello

Trained at Chetham’s School of Music and the Royal College of Music. He has toured worldwide with the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and held principal positions with RTE National Symphony Orchestra.

Anando Mukerjee

Tenor & vocals

Acclaimed tenor trained at Delhi and Cambridge Universities and under Nicolai Gedda. He has performed at Wigmore Hall, Cadogan Hall and the Royal Albert Hall.

Day by day

Six days, ending on a public stage

26 Oct

Initial assessment and goal setting

  • Welcome and registration
  • Introductions, orientation, initial assessment
27 Oct

Skill development and repertoire work

  • Individual lessons and practice clinics
28 Oct

Listening, blend and ensemble discipline

  • Group coaching and collaborative rehearsal
29 Oct

Musical interpretation and confidence building

  • Rehearsal and interpretation
  • Performance preparation and stagecraft
30 Oct

Dress rehearsal and performance readiness

  • Showcase preparation
  • Final rehearsal, reflection and concert briefing
31 Oct

Public performance and closing session

  • Programme reflection and celebration
  • Final showcase
